proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, 7^n is congruent to 7^(n mod 10) modulo 11.

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, n^2 is at least n.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 60 for which n^2 > 20.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, if n mod 2 = 1 then (n^2) mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 1001 modulo 77.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 50, 7^(n+10) mod 11 is congruent to 7^(n) mod 11 modulo 11.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, (n-4)*(2*n^2) equals (n-4)*((2*n^2) + [n = 4]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 143 modulo 13.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.

For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, at least one of the following holds: n mod 10 = 0; n mod 10 = 1; n mod 10 = 2; n mod 10 = 3; n mod 10 = 4; n mod 10 = 5; n mod 10 = 6; n mod 10 = 7; n mod 10 = 8; n mod 10 = 9.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, if n mod 10 = 0 then 7^(n) mod 11 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, n*(n+1) is at least 2*n.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 60 for which n^3 > 15.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, at least one of the following holds: n mod 4 = 0; n mod 4 = 1; n mod 4 = 2; n mod 4 = 3.
The steps above establish the statement up to 60, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 60.
